title: Find the invoice mistakes that distort a restaurant’s food costs
summary: A restaurant receives supplier invoices with inconsistent descriptions, pack sizes and occasional extraction errors. Give the owner an exception inbox showing which cost changes need checking and the original evidence behind each flag.
audience: Independent restaurant operators and their bookkeepers
buyer: Owner or bookkeeper responsible for reconciling supplier costs
flow: Check duplicates, pack sizes and price changes
deliverable: An interactive invoice exception inbox with an auditable correction history
question: Can an exception-first review reduce checking time without hiding genuine invoice errors?
measure: Known-error recall, false flags per invoice and correction time against a spreadsheet on a clearly labelled fixture set; real usefulness requires an operator trial.
baseline: Mindee already extracts invoice line items; xtraCHEF already offers restaurant invoice automation. A generic OCR app would duplicate existing products.
proposed_difference: Test a lightweight, locally processed exception review for operators who cannot justify a full purchasing platform. This segment and gap are hypotheses.
risk: Stop if operators already solve this cheaply, cannot supply consented examples, or correction time exceeds spreadsheet review. Do not promise accounting accuracy.
data_plan: Week one: bundled synthetic invoices and editable extracted CSV/JSON. Later: consented, redacted Swedish supplier invoices; no scraping private documents.
model_plan: Rules for totals and duplicate rows; optional small pretrained text embeddings for product matching only after exact matching baseline. PDF OCR is a later extension.
why_ml: Matching varied supplier descriptions may benefit from embeddings; arithmetic and duplicate checks should use rules.
venture: Potential narrow food-operations product or managed onboarding service; recurring value would come from verified cost history, not one-off OCR.
customer_test: Owner can test the inbox with two local operators/bookkeepers and ask which flags change an actual purchasing or correction decision.
week_test: In 4–6 days build CSV import, seeded duplicate/pack-size cases, side-by-side source view, corrections and export. No bank/POS integration or automated supplier disputes.
growth_path: Exception inbox → supplier-specific matching learned from corrections → repeatable onboarding for small operators.
evidence: A vendor feedback report describes duplicated extracted rows (search-index evidence; full page fetch timed out). Vendor material describes line-item and restaurant review problems. These are biased, limited signals, not validated local demand.
evidence_level: User report + vendor evidence; local demand untested
market: Evidence review pending; no automatic build

question: Does threshold calibration or limited adaptation improve reliability under lighting shift at a fixed false-alarm budget?

alternative: Frozen features + nearest-neighbour anomaly score; simple image statistics; an existing Anomalib baseline.

risk: Prior work may already answer the question; industrial images do not establish performance on a customer’s production line.

model_plan: Pretrained vision backbone; frozen features first, a small adapter only if feasible.
why_ml: Visual variability is hard to encode with fixed thresholds, but simple statistics may still win.

contribution: A small-data robustness study with explicit failure boundaries
feasibility: Start with a small public-data feasibility check on the laptop. Record licences, memory and runtime before scaling; no paid compute.

title: Does a contamination detector confuse familiarity with prior exposure?

question: Under a fixed local compute budget, how reliably do adaptation-based audits separate deliberately exposed sequences from new same-process sequences?
experiment: Use small, dated synthetic series generated after model release and controlled adaptations with known exposure. Compare static loss, candidate-only probes and reference-debiased probes. difference: The proposed test targets known adaptation exposure versus new same-process samples under a small compute budget. Whether this adds anything beyond existing ablations must be established first.
kill: Drop if existing code already covers the proposed distinction, controlled ground truth cannot isolate the factor, or even the smallest probe exceeds laptop resources.

title: A forecast pilot report a customer can actually challenge
intro: Package one model pilot so a customer can inspect data dates, baseline fairness, uncertainty and known disclosure gaps before accepting a headline accuracy claim.
why_now: October’s small-model release and linked evaluation discussion show why a model ranking alone leaves important questions unanswered.
flow: Check dates, baselines and missing disclosures
question: Does a transparent pilot report help a prospective custom-model customer choose between a simple baseline and adapting a pretrained model?
experiment: Use fev outputs or a small equivalent baseline run; separate measured outcomes from supplied metadata. Display model-release date, target dates, model hash, evaluation window, latency and uncertainty. Missing corpus disclosure stays unknown.
data: First ship an honest sample report with synthetic data and real baseline calculations. Any pretrained run must pass licence and CPU timing checks; never populate model results with invented predictions.
first_week: Deliver a local data import → baseline evaluation → evidence report in 4–6 days. The finished slice is one decision report, not a leaderboard or training platform.
venture: Possible entry deliverable for a custom-model consultancy. Buyer access and value are untested; a client conversation is necessary before building recurring infrastructure.
alternatives: fev already provides tasks and summaries; post-release evaluations already exist. Existing tooling should do the numerical work. Generic forecast dashboards are not the opportunity.
difference: A proposed client-facing interpretation and evidence layer around an existing evaluation. No novel metric or contamination detector is claimed.
kill: Drop if existing fev reports answer the customer’s questions, no customer will share a usable dataset, or the report does not change a decision.
scope: One-week service prototype. No API fees, GPU provisioning or paid model access.
confidence: Timely technical need; product gap and demand unvalidated
